entries.name: Versus Split Screen
entries.summary: A vs B: the screen splits into two colored halves, each side gets a name and image, then stat rows race head-to-head with a winner marker per row and a verdict. For rivalries, products, eras, countries, athletes.

entries.name: Data Story: Animated Bars
entries.summary: Numbers tell the story: a headline stat counts up, then labelled bars grow and re-sort while a takeaway line lands. For country comparisons, prices, records, survey results, market share.

entries.name: Archival Street Documentary
entries.summary: Period documentary: the camera travels up an old street (scene photos or a drawn one-point-perspective street) under a film grade, with typed archive date slips, film strip and projector wear. For any historical place or event.

title.description: Opening title card, a few words.

place.description: City or place name, shown small in capitals.

plates.description: One {date, label} per narration scene, in order.

date.description: Date stamp for this scene: a day, a year or an era ("c. 1890").

label.description: Short line under the date: the place or what the viewer sees.

grade.description: Period grade: silver (black and white), sepia, cyanotype (blue) or amber (tinted film).

street.description: Drawn street for scenes with no image: tramway (rails, wires, clock tower), boulevard (wide, trees, dome) or lane (narrow, lanterns, arch).

frame.description: Picture border: film (sprocket strip), print (mounted photo) or none.

showCaptions.description: Show word captions of the narration.

entries.name: Ink-Wash Moon Documentary
entries.summary: A space documentary painted in ink wash: a moon (or sun, or ringed planet) rises over misty peaks and changes phase each chapter, while vertical inscriptions, red seals and a brush-drawn ensō circle frame images and counted figures.

title.description: Opening title written over the moonrise, e.g. "Our Moon", "Why the Moon Has Phases".

subtitle.description: Small italic line under the title, e.g. "4.5 billion years beside the Earth". Can be empty.

heading.description: Short chapter heading, set vertically beside the sky like a scroll inscription, e.g. "The Giant Impact", "Apollo 11", "Tidal Lock".

phase.description: How the sky body looks in this chapter. For the moon: new, waxing-crescent, first-quarter, waxing-gibbous, full, waning-gibbous, last-quarter, waning-crescent, or eclipse (a red, eclipsed full moon). For the sun only "eclipse" changes it (a total solar eclipse).

stat.description: Optional figure shown inside a brush-drawn ink circle. null for none. When the scene has an image, the image fills the circle instead and the figure sits under it.

value.description: The number that counts up, e.g. 384400. Put years in the label or heading, not here.

unit.description: Short unit after the number, e.g. "km", "days", "%".

label.description: Small line under the number, e.g. "average distance from Earth".

chapters.description: One chapter per narration scene, in order. The first chapter shows after the title card.

orb.description: The body hanging in the painted sky: moon (phases work), sun (glowing disc; "eclipse" = total eclipse), ringed-planet (a banded planet with rings, like Saturn; phases shade it).

scenery.description: The ink landscape under the sky: mountains = layered peaks over a still lake; sea = far islands over open water; hills = low rolling hills and a lake.

palette.description: rice-paper = warm paper with black ink and a red seal (light); indigo-night = blue-black night with stars and gold; ember-dusk = dark plum dusk with amber light.

entries.name: Mosaic Reveal Documentary
entries.summary: Art-history documentary: glass and gold tesserae fly in and click into place to build each scene's image or a drawn motif, with a museum label per scene. For myths, sacred symbols, religious art and art history.

title.description: Gallery title shown at the top, a few words. Empty to hide.

label.description: Museum-label title of this scene, 1-6 words.

note.description: One short line under the label: place, date or meaning.

motif.description: Drawn mosaic for scenes without an image: sun, moon, star, tree, bird, fish, waves, halo (figure with a halo), eye, lotus or rosette.

panels.description: One {label, note, motif} per narration scene, in order.

palette.description: byzantine (gold ground, lapis, red), lapis (night blue with gold stars), roman (marble, terracotta, black) or cathedral (stained glass jewel tones).

tiles.description: Tile size: fine (detailed), medium or bold (big chunky tiles).

assembly.description: How tiles arrive: swirl (spiral in), sweep (stream from a corner), rise (from below), scatter (settle from everywhere) or mixed (changes every scene).

showCaptions.description: Show word captions of the narration.

entries.name: Line-Art Geography Lesson
entries.summary: Classroom-style geography explainer in ink line art on paper: a sketched spinning globe with pressure belts and wind rows, land-and-sea cross-sections, layered strata and comparison panels, drawn step by step with the narration.

chapter.description: Small course label shown above the title and beside each heading, e.g. "Geography · Unit 4".

title.description: Lesson title, e.g. "How the atmosphere moves heat".

subtitle.description: Optional line under the title, e.g. a second-language title or a one-line question.

heading.description: Chapter heading for this step, e.g. "The three-cell model". *Asterisks* colour a word.

diagram.description: globe = sketched Earth with latitude belts and wind rows; section = side-view cross-section of land and sky with arrows; layers = stacked strata (Earth interior, atmosphere, soil); panels = 2–4 side-by-side sketch cards comparing places or types.

label.description: Short name drawn on the diagram, e.g. "Equatorial low", "Trade winds", "Mantle", "Windward side".

detail.description: Optional small second line under the label, e.g. "rising air, heavy rain" or "about 2,900 km thick".

at.description: Where the mark sits. globe: latitude in degrees (-90 south pole … 0 equator … 90 north pole). section: position across the drawing, 0 (left) to 100 (right). layers: relative thickness of the layer (e.g. 1, 2, 5). panels: ignored.

tone.description: Line colour: warm (red/orange: heat, low pressure, rising air), cool (blue: cold, high pressure, sinking air, water), green (land, plants, winds), ink (neutral).

arrow.description: Movement drawn with the mark. globe: east/west = a row of wind or current arrows at that latitude, up/down = toward the north/south pole, none = a latitude line (belt, zone or boundary). section: up/down = rising/sinking arrow, east/west = sideways flow. panels: a small arrow beside the label.

icon.description: Line icon, only used by the panels diagram (sun, cloud, rain, drop, leaf, mountain, wave, globe, map, pin, fire, house, building, people...).

marks.description: 1–6 labelled parts of the diagram, in the order the narration mentions them (panels use the first 4).

note.description: Optional one-line handwritten takeaway under the diagram, e.g. "Rising air cools, so clouds form here".

steps.description: 1–8 lesson steps in order, one per narration line (an extra first narration line becomes the title card).

palette.description: paper = cream page with ink lines (the classic lesson look), blueprint = navy with white lines, chalk = green chalkboard.

showCaptions.description: Word-synced subtitles in a plate at the bottom.

entries.name: Money Story: Value Line Explainer
entries.summary: Tells a money concept in illustrated beats while a glowing price/value line draws itself and reacts to each beat: it rises or falls, a counter ticks, the change lands as a badge. For prices, inflation, markets, savings, money history.

title.description: The money story in a few words, e.g. "Gold after the dollar left it". Opening title and header.

metric.description: What the value line measures and how its numbers are formatted.

label.description: What the line measures, e.g. "Gold, US$ per troy ounce".

suffix.description: Written after every number, e.g. "%" or " bn".

label.description: Short time marker shown on the chart axis, e.g. "1971" or "Day 3". Max 10 characters.

headline.description: What happened at this moment, in at most 9 words. Wrap one key word in *asterisks* to highlight it.

value.description: The tracked number at this moment (a price, a balance, an index). Real data only.

note.description: Optional tag pinned to this point on the chart, e.g. "Record high". Max 28 characters.

icon.description: Line icon drawn for this beat, e.g. money, chart, building, fire, globe, clock, lock, shield.

beats.description: 2-7 story beats in time order, one per narration scene. One extra first scene becomes the title card.

takeaway.description: One closing sentence shown over the last beat. Leave empty for none.

source.description: Where the numbers come from, shown small under the chart.

palette.description: amber = warm black and gold, ledger = light paper and green ink, mint = dark green terminal, midnight = deep blue and cyan.

showCaptions.description: Show the narration as word captions at the bottom.

entries.name: Pipeline Schematic Explainer
entries.summary: Dark technical-schematic explainer: a pipeline of glowing modules on a rail pans stage by stage while bullets, a counter card and a bottom stepper explain how a film, song, game or show gets made.

kicker.description: Small series label above the title, e.g. "How it's made · Animation".

title.description: Title of the explainer, e.g. "How an *animated film* is made".

subtitle.description: Optional one line under the title.

name.description: Short stage name shown on the diagram module and the bottom stepper, e.g. "Storyboard", "Recording", "Mixing".

icon.description: Line icon drawn inside the module (camera, music, book, chat, people, star, trophy, chip, gear, bulb, calendar, ...).

tag.description: Optional small mono line under the stage name, e.g. "months 1-6" or "story team".

stages.description: 2-6 stages of the process, left to right. They form the diagram pipeline and the bottom stepper.

stage.description: Which stage (1-based, in `stages` order) this step is about. Leave out to use the step order.

heading.description: Headline of this step, e.g. "Every shot starts as a *sketch*". *Asterisks* colour a word.

points.description: 1-3 short bullet lines, in the order the narration says them.

stat.description: Optional key number for this step, shown as a counter card under the bullets.

value.description: The number that counts up, e.g. 24. Real and checkable only.

decimals.description: Decimal places shown for the value.

unit.description: Short unit after the number, e.g. "fps", "%", "min".

label.description: What the number means, e.g. "frames in every second of film".

steps.description: 1-8 steps, one per narration line (an extra first narration line becomes the title card).

flowLabel.description: Optional name of what flows through the pipeline, shown on the moving packets, e.g. "Shots", "Tracks", "Scenes".

palette.description: midnight = deep navy with electric blue (the classic schematic look), graphite = near-black with orange, studio = light grey with blue.

entries.name: Route Trace Explainer
entries.summary: Sports course explainer: a glowing GPS-style line traces a marathon, race stage, track or trail over topographic terrain as the camera follows the runner, with checkpoint cards, live stats and a profile strip.

title.description: Name of the route or course, e.g. "The Boston Marathon course".

kicker.description: Small label above the title, e.g. "MARATHON · POINT TO POINT".

unit.description: Distance unit for `total` and every checkpoint `at`.

total.description: Full route length in `unit`, e.g. 42.2 or 26.2.

route.description: How the route line is drawn. It is a stylised trace, not a survey map.

shape.description: Overall form of the drawn route: loop (back to start), point-to-point (A to B), out-and-back, figure-eight, or circuit (race track).

points.description: Optional rough trace of the real route as 3–24 points on a 0–100 grid (y grows downward). Leave empty to use `shape`.

at.description: Distance from the start where this checkpoint sits, in `unit` (e.g. 21 for mile 21). Must be ≤ total.

label.description: Short place or moment name, e.g. "Heartbreak Hill", "Turn 1", "Summit".

note.description: One factual line about this stretch, e.g. "Last of four climbs through Newton".

icon.description: Line icon on the checkpoint card (flag, mountain, trophy, clock, fire, wave, building, star, target...).

elevation.description: Height above sea level at this point (metres for km, feet for mi). Leave out when unknown; the profile only draws with 2+ values.

checkpoints.description: 2–8 points along the route in order of distance, one per narration line. Usually starts at 0 and ends at the finish.

palette.description: night = navy with orange route, track = black with lime route, glacier = light with red route.

entries.name: Step-by-Step Diagram Explainer
entries.summary: Explains a process as connected step cards that draw themselves: numbered nodes, arrows that animate between them, the active step highlighted while narration covers it. For how things work, scientific processes, workflows, tutorials.

entries.name: Countdown Listicle
entries.summary: Top-N countdown: a giant rank number crashes in, then the item title and one-line why, over the scene image or a bold color field. For rankings, facts, tips, 'N things you didn't know'.

entries.name: Map Country Tour
entries.summary: A country or city tour on a stylised map: the camera follows a car, train or plane along a drawn route, pins drop at each stop and a place card shows a flat illustration, a counted-up stat and one fact.

title.description: Opening title, e.g. "Japan in five stops". Wrap one word in *asterisks* to colour it.

subtitle.description: Small line above the title, e.g. "5 stops · 1 journey". Leave empty to show the number of stops and the total distance.

name.description: Place name shown on the card and the pin, e.g. "Kyoto", "Mount Fuji", "Old Town".

region.description: Small label above the name: province, state or district, e.g. "Kansai", "Hokkaido". Can be empty.

lat.description: Latitude in decimal degrees (north positive), e.g. 35.01. Places the pin on the stylised map.

lon.description: Longitude in decimal degrees (east positive), e.g. 135.77.

fact.description: One short, verifiable fact about the place, shown on its card.

stat.description: Optional headline number for the card (counts up). null when there is no good number.

unit.description: Short unit or label after the number, e.g. "m high", "years as capital".

scenery.description: Flat illustration at the top of the card: city skyline, mountains, coast, forest, desert dunes, countryside fields, or oldtown (colourful historic houses).

icon.description: Line icon next to the stat or fact (e.g. building, mountain, wave, leaf, star, flag).

stops.description: 2–8 stops in travel order. All in one country, region or city, so the map stays readable.

travel.description: How the route is drawn: flight = dashed arcs with a plane, road = curving road with a car, rail = rail line with a train.

units.description: Units of the distance counter (straight-line distance between stops).

palette.description: sunset = warm dark terracotta, atlas = light paper atlas, night = deep navy with mint, jungle = deep green with gold.

entries.name: Match Recap Scoreboard
entries.summary: Broadcast-style match recap: score bug slams in, a minute-by-minute event ticker (goals, cards, subs) drives the score, then key stats compare both teams. For football, basketball, any scored sport.

entries.name: News City Blocks
entries.summary: Geography news recap on a miniature isometric city: each story is a tower with a place pin; the camera flies tower to tower while a card shows region, headline and a figure, under a live ticker. Map changes, world desk roundups.

title.description: Recap title, at most ~6 words, e.g. "The year the map changed".

edition.description: Edition or period, e.g. "World desk · 2022". Empty to hide.

place.description: Where it happened, short: a city, country or region, e.g. "Astana, Kazakhstan".

region.description: Short region or beat chip, e.g. "CENTRAL ASIA", "EUROPE", "BORDERS".

headline.description: Headline, at most ~8 words, e.g. "Kazakhstan renames its capital back to Astana".

detail.description: One short sentence of context (under 18 words). Empty to hide.

icon.description: Icon in the place pin: pin, flag, building, map, globe, mountain, wave, car...

figure.description: Optional real, checkable number for this story. Leave out rather than guess.

label.description: What the number measures, e.g. "years after independence".

stories.description: 2-6 stories. Narration: an optional intro scene, then one scene per story.

timeOfDay.description: City lighting: day (light), dusk (violet/orange) or night (navy, lit windows).

entries.name: News Headline Highlighter
entries.summary: A newspaper-style article card slides in, the camera pushes toward the headline and a marker highlights key phrases one by one, then a 'why it matters' card. For news recaps, announcements, studies, historical front pages.

entries.name: News Roundup Cards
entries.summary: A fast roundup deck: one broadcast-style card per story with category and date chips, a big headline, a one-line takeaway, numbered points and a counting figure, swapped by an accent wipe. Releases, launches, any news beat.

title.description: Roundup title, e.g. "This week in film" (at most ~6 words).

period.description: Period covered, e.g. "Sep 25-26" or "November 2004". Empty to hide.

headline.description: Headline of this story, at most ~7 words (a title, product or event name works).

date.description: Release or event date as display text, e.g. "Nov 9, 2004". Empty to hide.

takeaway.description: One sentence: the single thing to remember about this story.

points.description: 0-3 short supporting facts, each under 9 words.

icon.description: Icon for the side panel (used when the scene has no image).

figure.description: Optional key number for the story. Only real, checkable numbers.

unit.description: Shown after the number, e.g. "M" or "%".

label.description: What the number measures, e.g. "first-day sales".

source.description: Where the facts come from, e.g. "Source: Nintendo". Empty to hide.

stories.description: 2-8 stories. Narration: an optional intro scene, then one scene per story.

palette.description: Colour scheme: midnight (navy/cyan), graphite (black/orange), violet (purple/lime) or paper (light).

entries.name: Kinetic Quote
entries.summary: A quote or bold statement revealed word by word in large editorial serif type, with the key words highlighted and the attribution signed at the end. For famous quotes, scripture, philosophy, hot takes.

entries.name: Sports App Showreel
entries.summary: Fast showreel for a sports app or fan product: a phone flies in and launches the app, then each shot swings the camera to a new screen (live scores, stat bars, fan vote, comments, a big highlight number) under a kinetic headline.

appName.description: Product or app name shown in the app header and on the launch splash.

icon.description: App icon glyph (ball, trophy, flag, target, chart...).

title.description: Opening hook while the app launches, ≤ 7 words. *asterisks* colour a word.

tagline.description: Optional product line that slides in under the phone on the last shot.

headline.description: Kinetic headline above the phone, ≤ 7 words. Wrap 1–2 words in *asterisks* to colour them.

screen.description: App screen shown in the phone: scores = live/result list, stats = ranked bars, vote = pick tiles + button, feed = fan comments, highlight = one big number over a pitch or the scene image.

heading.description: Title of the app screen, e.g. "Results", "Golden Boot", "Your pick".

label.description: Main text of the row. scores: "Team A vs Team B"; stats/vote: a player or team name; feed: the user name; highlight: what the number counts ("Fans at the final").

sub.description: Second line. scores: stage or status ("Final", "78'"); vote: team or award; feed: the message itself; highlight: where/when.

value.description: Short value shown on the right or as the big number: "3–3", "8", "88,966", "now". Plain numbers count up.

bar.description: Optional 0–100 bar length (share, progress, rating). Leave out when there is nothing to compare.

rows.description: 1–5 rows of the screen, most important first (the first row is the one the finger taps).

button.description: Optional button at the bottom of the screen ("Vote", "Follow team"); best on vote screens.

shots.description: One shot per narration scene. With one more scene than shots, scene 0 is the launch intro.

palette.description: volt = lime on black, court = orange, ice = cyan, turf = green.

entries.name: Cosmic Scale Ladder
entries.summary: Bodies of wildly different sizes appear side by side while the camera pulls back by orders of magnitude over a starfield, with a size readout. For 'how big is X': planets, cells, buildings.

entries.name: Cartoon Explainer: Host and Props
entries.summary: A Saturday-morning cartoon explainer: an outlined SVG host walks past rolling hills, and each step's cartoon prop drops in, acts out the idea and can poof into another. For science and kids' how-it-works topics.

title.description: Episode title, e.g. "Where does rain come from?". Shown on the opening title card.

host.description: The cartoon host who acts out every step.

kind.description: The cartoon host: blob (round friendly creature), robot, or professor (lab coat, glasses).

name.description: Optional host name shown on the title card, e.g. "Professor Pip".

heading.description: What happens in this step, in at most 6 words, e.g. "Heat melts the ice". Wrap one word in *asterisks* to colour it.

line.description: Short line the host says in a speech bubble (max 70 characters). Leave empty for no bubble.

prop.description: Cartoon prop acting out the step: sun, cloud, drop, ice, flame, plant, tree, atom, dna, cell, heart, magnet, bolt, bulb, battery, thermometer, flask, rocket, planet, moon, earth.

becomes.description: Optional: the prop changes into this prop halfway through the step, e.g. ice becomes drop. "none" keeps it.

action.description: What the host does: point (at the prop), explain (open arms), think (hand on chin), wave, cheer (jumps), shock (surprised jump).

sfx.description: Optional comic sound word next to the prop, e.g. "POP!", "ZAP!", "DRIP!". Max 8 characters.

steps.description: 2-7 steps in order, one per narration scene. Add one extra first scene to get a title card.

takeaway.description: Optional closing idea shown at the end of the last step, e.g. "Same water, three *states*!". Leave empty for none.

palette.description: saturday = bright sky and green hills, dusk = purple sunset, chalk = soft paper colours.

showCaptions.description: Show the narration as word captions on the ground band.

entries.name: Sketchbook Dialogue: Two-Character Tech Story
entries.summary: A 2D sketchbook short: two drawn characters (developer, founder, scientist, robot) trade lines in speech bubbles while a magic pencil sketches each set and idea. For tech origin stories and conversations.

title.description: Story title, e.g. "The bug that only happened on Fridays". Shown on the opening title card and in the corner label.

name.description: Short character name shown on their speech bubbles, e.g. "Maya" or "Bit".

style.description: Outfit: hoodie (developer, glasses), blazer (founder or manager), labcoat (scientist or engineer), cap (student or maker, t-shirt and cap), robot (an AI or machine).

color.description: Main outfit colour: olive, navy, coral, teal, plum, charcoal or mustard.

skin.description: Skin tone: light, tan, brown or deep. Ignored for the robot.

cast.description: One or two characters. The first stands on the left (speaker "a"), the second on the right (speaker "b").

speaker.description: Who says this line: "a" (first cast member, left), "b" (second, right) or "narrator" (a caption strip at the top, no bubble).

line.description: The spoken line shown in the speech bubble, at most 90 characters. Usually the same words as this scene's narration, or a short version of it.

place.description: Set sketched behind the cast: paper (blank page), desk (desk and monitor), city (skyline), servers (server racks), sky (sunset clouds on a paper plane), night (dark room under the stars).

sketch.description: Optional object the pencil draws in a glowing loop between the characters, e.g. code, chip, lock, cloud, rocket, brain, bulb, phone, globe. "none" for no object.

action.description: What the speaker does: talk, point (at the sketch), think, shrug, wave, cheer (jump with arms up) or shock. For narrator beats, both characters do it.

beats.description: 2-8 story beats in order, one per narration scene. Add one extra first narration scene to get a title card.

timer.description: Show a small countdown clock in the top corner (time left in the story).

palette.description: sketchbook = warm paper and orange, pastel = cool paper and blue, blueprint = dark navy with light lines.

showCaptions.description: Also show the narration as word captions under the stage. Leave off when the bubbles already show the same words.

entries.name: Chat Thread Story
entries.summary: A story told as a phone chat: bubbles pop in with typing indicators, timestamps and a twist message at the end. For relatable stories, dialogues, historical 'what if they texted', customer stories.

entries.name: Cosmic Zoom-Out
entries.summary: One continuous camera pull-back from a place on Earth through planet, orbits, stars and galaxies to the observable universe, with a 'you are here' marker, a size readout per level and a scale ruler.

title.description: Opening line over the first level. Wrap one word in *asterisks* to highlight it.

homeLabel.description: Label of the marker that keeps pointing at the starting place.

name.description: Short name of this scale level, e.g. "The Milky Way".

span.description: Size or distance readout, e.g. "about 100,000 light-years across".

note.description: One extra fact line shown under the readout. May be empty.

view.description: Drawing for this level: surface, planet, orbit, system, stars, galaxy, group or web.

labels.description: Up to 4 names pinned on the drawing, e.g. ["Andromeda", "Triangulum"].

levels.description: 3 to 8 scale levels, smallest first. One narration scene per level.

palette.description: deep (blue), aurora (green), ember (warm) or mono (black and white).

showRuler.description: Show the scale ruler along the bottom.

entries.name: Dev Session Diary
entries.summary: A tech story told as one working session at a cartoon desk: timestamped chat bubbles type out, the character reacts, the monitor shows errors, builds and wins, the wall clock turns and the window goes from day to night.

title.description: Opening line typed on the monitor while the camera pulls back, ≤ 40 characters.

nameplate.description: Text on the desk nameplate, ≤ 28 characters (a name or a role). "" hides the plate text.

human.description: Name shown on human bubbles, e.g. "Dev" or "Operator".

machine.description: Name shown on machine bubbles, e.g. "Terminal" or "Build bot".

time.description: Clock time of the moment, "HH:MM" (24h), e.g. "09:14". Use "" if unknown.

message.description: The message or log line for this moment, ≤ 90 characters, e.g. "Why does the login page loop forever?"

who.description: "human" = the person at the desk says it; "machine" = the computer replies (mono terminal bubble).

screen.description: Monitor state: typing (terminal), thinking (idea bulb), progress (bar fills), error (red cross), success (green check), chart (growth), launch (rocket).

sticker.description: Optional ribbon slapped on the character, e.g. "SO COOL" or "BUG FOUND". Use "" for none.

beats.description: 2–12 moments of the session in time order, one per narration scene.

sky.description: Window light across the video: day-to-night, night-to-dawn, or daylight only.

palette.description: Room colours: cozy (cream and teal), pastel (lilac), midnight (dark navy).

showCaptions.description: Show word captions at the bottom.

entries.name: Pixel Arcade Story
entries.summary: A 16-bit side-scroller that tells a story as game levels: a pixel hero runs through parallax worlds, jumps hazards and collects coins, with a dialog box per level, score/lives HUD and a stage-clear finale.

title.description: Game title on the start screen, e.g. "The Water Cycle". Wrap one word in *asterisks* to highlight it.

hero.description: Pixel character: runner (orange critter), astronaut, robot or cat.

name.description: Level title shown in the dialog box, e.g. "Evaporation" or "The Moon Landing".

text.description: One short line the level teaches or tells (a fact or a story beat). Shown in the dialog box.

world.description: Background world the character runs through.

hazard.description: What the character jumps over. "auto" picks one that suits the world.

item.description: What the character collects (coin 100, star 250, gem 500, heart 50 points).

hit.description: true = the character gets hit once in this level and loses a life (a setback in the story).

levels.description: 2–8 levels in story order; each one usually matches one narration scene.

ending.description: Banner on the final screen, e.g. "STAGE CLEAR", "MISSION COMPLETE", "GAME OVER".

palette.description: nebula = purple space night, gameboy = 4-shade green handheld, sunset = warm pink dusk, arcade = black with neon.

entries.name: Rain Mood Story
entries.summary: A calm, moody 2D illustrated short: layered parallax landscapes (forest, mountains, lake, coast, city, station, field) under rain, storms, snow or fog, with silhouette figures, location tags and quiet serif captions.

title.description: Opening title, max ~6 words. Wrap one word in *asterisks* to tint it.

subtitle.description: Small line under the title: a place, season or mood.

setting.description: Drawn place: forest, mountains, lake, coast (sea + lighthouse), city (rainy streets), station (train platform) or field.

weather.description: rain, storm (heavy rain + lightning), snow, fog or clear (fireflies/dust).

figure.description: none, umbrella (person under an umbrella), walker, deer or birds (a flock crossing the sky).

label.description: Short place or moment tag, max 40 characters. Empty shows nothing.

shots.description: One shot per narration scene, in order. Extra scenes reuse the shots from the start.

closing.description: Quiet closing line shown over the last scene, e.g. "Listen to it fall." Empty shows nothing.

mood.description: Colour mood: blue-hour (cool blues, warm lamps), ember (warm), moss (green, earthy), mono (near black and white).

showCaptions.description: Show the narration as calm word captions.

entries.name: Company History Timeline
entries.summary: Company or product history, milestone by milestone: an odometer year badge, a date chip and one card per milestone (founding document, spotlit product shot, growth stat or parent-company chart) over a travelling year rail.

company.description: Company or product name shown in the year badge, e.g. "Nintendo".

title.description: Opening title, e.g. "From playing cards to *Switch*". Wrap one word in *asterisks* to colour it.

year.description: Year of the milestone, e.g. 1998. The year badge rolls to it and the rail travels to it.

date.description: Exact date shown on the date chip, e.g. "September 4, 1998". Leave empty to show just the year.

tag.description: One or two words saying what happened: "Founded", "Launched", "Acquired", "IPO", "Renamed", "Record".

headline.description: Short title of the milestone, usually a name: "Google Inc.", "The iPhone", "Alphabet".

detail.description: One plain sentence explaining the milestone.

card.description: How the milestone is shown: document = founding certificate / press-release paper; product = spotlit product shot or logo (uses the image of the narration scene playing at that moment, else the icon); stat = big growth number from `stat`; branch = parent box splitting into `branches` (mergers, spin-offs, new parent company).

stat.description: Required when card is "stat". Ignored otherwise.

value.description: The number that counts up, e.g. 118.69 or 1000000.

prefix.description: Text before the number, e.g. "$". Usually empty.

label.description: What the number measures, e.g. "units sold worldwide".

branches.description: 2–3 names under the headline when card is "branch", e.g. ["Google", "Other Bets"].

stamp.description: Optional rubber stamp slammed on the card, e.g. "PUBLIC", "SOLD OUT", "ANTITRUST". Usually empty.

icon.description: Line icon used on document seals and for product cards with no image (e.g. building, rocket, phone, chip, cart, money).

milestones.description: 3–10 milestones in chronological order, oldest first.

palette.description: studio = clean light grey with soft colour, boardroom = deep navy night, heritage = warm paper and ink.

entries.name: Deep-Time Era Ruler
entries.summary: Travels through geological periods, prehistoric ages or dynasties: an era card with a drawn illustration, over a colour-banded era ruler that zooms into each era while a date pin counts through it.

title.description: Opening title, e.g. "From the dinosaurs to the first farmers". Wrap one word in *asterisks* to colour it.

axis.description: years-ago = deep time (geology, prehistory) on a logarithmic ruler; calendar = dated history (dynasties, empires) on a linear ruler.

kicker.description: Small label above the name: the larger period or group, e.g. "Mesozoic Era", "Imperial China". Can be empty.

name.description: Name of the era, epoch, period or dynasty, e.g. "Jurassic", "Tang dynasty".

from.description: When the era starts. In "years-ago" axis: years before present (201000000). In "calendar" axis: calendar year, negative for BC (618).

to.description: When the era ends, same unit as `from` (0 = today in "years-ago" axis).

span.description: Readable date range shown under the name, e.g. "201–145 million years ago", "618–907 AD".

points.description: 1–3 short facts about the era, revealed one by one as the narration goes.

visual.description: Illustration: globe = planet with drifting continents, strata = rock layers with this era highlighted, terrain = landscape cross-section with a water level, icon = a large drawn line icon.

icon.description: Line icon used when visual is "icon" (e.g. building, flag, book, fire, leaf, mountain).

eras.description: 2–10 eras in chronological order, oldest first.

palette.description: earth = warm dark brown, abyss = deep teal night, parchment = light paper.

entries.name: Doodle Civilization Timeline
entries.summary: Storybook doodle timeline: a lantern-carrying traveller walks across night hills while each milestone grows out of the ground as a paper medallion, year counting up; the last one hatches from an egg. For tech and invention history.

title.description: Opening title written over the night sky, e.g. "How computers *learned* to talk". Wrap one word in *asterisks* to colour it.

subtitle.description: Small line under the title, e.g. "A short history of the internet". Can be empty.

year.description: When it happened, as shown on screen: "1969", "1940s", "3000 BC". Plain 3–4 digit years count up from the previous one.

title.description: What appeared, in a few words: "First web page", "The transistor", "ARPANET".

detail.description: One short plain sentence explaining it. Can be empty.

icon.description: Doodle drawn on the milestone: chip, code, phone, globe, mail, rocket, bulb, brain, gear, book, camera, music, chat, lock, chart, atom, spark...

milestones.description: 3–9 milestones in chronological order, oldest first. The traveller walks from one to the next and each one grows out of the hills.

finale.description: How the LAST milestone arrives: hatch = an egg wobbles, cracks and hatches its doodle in a burst of light (a new era, a breakthrough); glow = it lights up the whole sky; none = like the others.

palette.description: night = starry blue storybook night, dusk = violet evening with warm glow, paper = light sketchbook paper with ink lines.

entries.name: Scrolling Timeline of Eras
entries.summary: A vertical timeline that scrolls through dated milestones: year counter, era bands, milestone cards with one-line facts. For history of X, evolution of a technology, eras of a civilization.

entries.name: Creator How-To
entries.summary: Warm, app-style how-to for film, music, games and hobby culture: a serif headline with a hand-drawn underline, a tip bubble and a floating task card whose checklist ticks off before a cursor taps the step's button.

title.description: What the viewer will learn, e.g. "How to care for your *vinyl*." Wrap 1–2 words in *asterisks*: they turn italic, accent-coloured and get a hand-drawn underline.

kicker.description: Small label in the top bar and above the title, e.g. "Record care" or "Film club basics".

label.description: Short name of the step, shown on the card header and in the intro list, e.g. "Store them upright".

headline.description: The instruction as a headline, e.g. "Keep them *standing*." *Asterisks* highlight 1–2 words.

items.description: 0–4 short checklist lines that tick off one by one, e.g. ["Shelf deep enough", "No leaning stacks"].

tip.description: One plain tip shown in a chat-style bubble, e.g. "Records stored flat warp under their own weight."

action.description: Label of the button a cursor taps at the end of the step, e.g. "Shelved", "Done", "Saved". "" = no button.

icon.description: Line icon for the step, e.g. music, camera, book, star, heart, clock, check, spark, calendar, people.

steps.description: The how-to in order, 2–6 steps. Narration: scene 1 is the title, then one scene per step.

palette.description: cream = warm paper with burnt-orange accent; blush = pink and sky with raspberry accent; studio = dark warm night with amber accent.

entries.name: Money Steps
entries.summary: Personal finance tutorial on a glowing money path: an orb travels node to node as each step's headline rises in, a hero figure counts up with a neon glow and glass chips show the supporting numbers.

title.description: What the tutorial teaches, e.g. "The *50/30/20* budget". Wrap 1–2 words in *asterisks* for the accent colour.

kicker.description: Small label above the title and in the top bar, e.g. "Money basics".

label.description: Short step name shown as "STEP 02 · LABEL", e.g. "Cover your needs".

headline.description: The instruction for this step, e.g. "Put *50%* toward needs". *Asterisks* highlight words.

detail.description: One plain supporting sentence, e.g. "Rent, groceries, insurance and minimum loan payments."

icon.description: Line icon on this step's node, e.g. money, chart, bars, calendar, clock, house, cart, shield, lock, target, check.

stat.description: Optional hero number for this step that counts up with a glow.

value.description: The number that counts up, e.g. 800 or 4.5. Plain number, no symbols.

prefix.description: Shown before the number, e.g. "$", "€", "£" or "".

suffix.description: Shown after the number, e.g. "%", "/mo", "k", " yrs" or "".

decimals.description: Digits after the decimal point (0 for whole amounts).

label.description: Small line above the number saying what it is, e.g. "goes to savings each month".

chips.description: 0–3 small glass chips with supporting figures.

value.description: Short figure on the glass chip, e.g. "$2,000", "50%", "3–6 mo".

label.description: One or two words under the figure, e.g. "needs", "per year".

steps.description: The method in order, 2–6 steps. Narration scene i+1 explains step i (scene 1 is the title).

palette.description: neon = black with lime glow; gold = black with warm gold; ocean = deep navy with cyan; ledger = light paper with green ink.

disclaimer.description: Small line in the top bar. Keep it for anything that sounds like advice; "" hides it.

entries.name: Glow Reel Steps
entries.summary: Fast neon motion-reel how-to for music, film, games and fan culture: warp-streak intro, HUD frame, a glowing icon emblem with orbiting sparkles and a terminal card that types each step and prints its checklist.

title.description: What the viewer will learn, e.g. "How to build a *perfect* playlist". Wrap 1–2 words in *asterisks* to light them in the accent colour.

kicker.description: Short topic label in the HUD corner and above the title, e.g. "Music basics" or "Film club".

label.description: Short step name, typed into the terminal card and listed in the intro, e.g. "Pick an opening track".

headline.description: The instruction as a punchy headline, e.g. "Open with *energy*." *Asterisks* light 1–2 words.

items.description: 0–3 short lines that print one by one under the command, e.g. ["Mid-tempo, not a ballad", "Instantly recognisable"].

icon.description: Line icon drawn inside the glowing emblem, e.g. music, camera, book, star, heart, people, calendar, clock, chat, trophy, spark.

steps.description: The how-to in order, 2–6 steps. Narration: scene 1 is the title, then one scene per step, then an optional finale scene.

finale.description: Closing line shown in a last narration scene after the steps, e.g. "Now press *play*." "" = no finale card.

palette.description: electric = vivid cobalt blue with ice-cyan accent; violet = ultraviolet purple with pink accent; night = deep teal-black with mint accent.

entries.name: Sports Play Steps
entries.summary: Step-by-step sports tutorial on an animated tactics board: players move along drawn run, dribble and pass arrows while a chaptered headline and a coaching-cue card explain each step. Basketball, soccer, football or a blank board.

title.description: Name of the play or drill, e.g. "The *pick and roll*". Wrap 1–2 words in *asterisks* to highlight them.

kicker.description: Small label shown above the title and in the top bar, e.g. "Basketball playbook".

field.description: Which playing surface the board draws (attacking end at the top). "plain" = a blank tactics board for any sport.

side.description: attack = filled accent marker; defense = outlined marker.

x.description: Start position: 0 = left sideline, 50 = centre, 100 = right sideline.

y.description: Start position: 0 = the goal / hoop end at the top, 100 = the far end at the bottom.

players.description: Everyone on the board at the start. Keep it readable: 2–10 markers.

ballWith.description: id of the player holding the ball at the start, or "" for no ball.

label.description: Short step name shown as "01 / LABEL", e.g. "Set the screen".

headline.description: The instruction for this step, e.g. "Plant a *solid screen*". *Asterisks* highlight words.

tip.description: One coaching cue in plain words, e.g. "Feet wide, arms in, stay still."

icon.description: Line icon on the cue card, e.g. target, arrow, person, people, ball, check, clock, star, trophy.

moves.description: Movements in this step. Positions carry over to the next step.

player.description: id of the player who moves.

kind.description: run = curved solid arrow; dribble = wavy arrow (use for the ball carrier).

passTo.description: After the moves, the ball carrier passes to this player id. "goal" = shot / score. "" = no pass.

steps.description: The play in order, 2–6 steps. Narration scene i+1 explains step i (scene 1 is the title).

palette.description: clean = white studio with blue accent; night = dark green floodlight; court = warm hardwood.

entries.name: Tech Stack Build
entries.summary: Graphite-studio tech tutorial: each step's voxels fly in and snap into a new layer of an orbiting 3D stack, with typed terminal commands, layer tags and a pipeline progress rail.

title.description: What the viewer builds, max 48 characters. Wrap ONE word in *asterisks* for the accent, e.g. "Build your first *Node.js* API".

command.description: Command typed in the intro terminal, max 44 characters, e.g. "mkdir hello-api". "" shows the title only.

label.description: Layer name, 1-2 words, max 12 characters, e.g. "Database". Shown on the stack tag and the progress rail.

title.description: The instruction, max 40 characters. Wrap 1-2 words in *asterisks* for the accent colour, e.g. "Add a *database*".

detail.description: One plain sentence on what this step does or why, max 110 characters. "" for none.

code.description: Optional command or one line of code typed into a terminal chip, max 40 characters, e.g. "npm install express". "" for none.

icon.description: Line icon on the layer tag: code, chip, gear, lock, shield, globe, rocket, cloud, chart, search, bars, check.

steps.description: 2-6 steps in order. Each step adds one layer to the 3D stack.

outro.description: Closing line on the recap scene, max 40 characters, with one *accent* word. "" reuses the title.

palette.description: slate = graphite studio with orange accent, midnight = deep navy with cyan, paper = light cream with red-orange.
